question:
Figure 1 and figure 2 are the same patch of ground photographed years apart, already co-registered. Report the location of the main building change as a normalized (x, y) coordinate, where (0, 0) is the top-left corner and (1, 1) the bottom-right corner. Which of the following is the centre of the changed area?
(A) (0.581, 0.242)
(B) (0.836, 0.842)
(C) (0.511, 0.742)
(D) (0.122, 0.760)

Answer with only the correct option letter.

<tool_call>

</tool_call>

After overlaying [img2] onto [img1], I can see a significant change in the bottom-left portion of the image. In [img2], there is a developed area with roads, buildings, and paved surfaces that did not exist in [img1]. This area is located around the (0.5, 0.7) to (0.7, 0.9) region.

The cropped view in [img6] still does not clearly show any building change. It appears to be a region of dirt and vegetation, similar to the other regions I've examined. This suggests that option (C) might not be correct either.

<tool_call>

<tool_call>

After resizing [img7] to a larger view in [img8], I can clearly see the building and paved area that was not present in [img1]. This region shows the most significant building change between the two images.

Therefore, the correct answer is (D).
